<thought>After several attempts to locate a commercially available precursor that can be converted to the target in a single step, the most straightforward one‑step transformation is the esterification of the corresponding carboxylic acid with methanol. The target is a methyl ester, so the retrosynthetic disconnection is:

COC(C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C)/C=C/C2=CC=CC=C2)=O  ←  esterification  →  O=C(O)C(C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C)/C=C/C2=CC=CC=C2)  +  CH₃OH

Both the carboxylic acid and methanol are commercially available and inexpensive (well under the $125 budget). The esterification can be performed in a single step (e.g., Fischer esterification or using a coupling reagent). The resulting retrosynthesis tree therefore has one reaction node and two leaf nodes that are buyable.</thought>
